notes: Hand-labeled ground truth for review-deps. Focused on STRUCTURAL hygiene defects (semver discipline, CI/SCA, lockfile, pinning policy) — these are stable over time. Specific-CVE findings would decay with the registry and are out of scope for this eval.

findings.summary: electron pinned to ^31.0.0 — Electron 31 reached end-of-life on the official support schedule before the current quarter; the ^ range cannot escape the 31.x line.
findings.evidence: devDependencies.electron = ^31.0.0; Electron's support window covers the latest 3 majors, and ^31.0.0 prevents adoption of 32+ without manual bump. CVEs published against earlier majors are typically backported only to supported lines.
findings.recommendation: Bump to the latest supported Electron major (verify against https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines) and re-test main/preload/renderer surface. Add a quarterly Electron-bump task to the maintenance cadence.

findings.summary: @anthropic-ai/sdk pinned at ^0.104.1 — per semver, ^0.x.y only allows 0.x.* patch updates. Any minor release (including security-relevant ones) requires a manual bump.
findings.evidence: dependencies['@anthropic-ai/sdk'] = ^0.104.1; pre-1.0 caret behavior in npm semver does not permit minor upgrades.
findings.recommendation: Either bump to the latest published 0.x or, if a 1.0 has been published, migrate. Document the SDK as 'manual minor bumps required' in the maintenance docs until 1.0.

findings.summary: No automated dependency audit is wired into CI — there is no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, .circleci, renovate.json, or dependabot config in the repo. Vulnerabilities published against pinned versions will be discovered only on manual inspection.
findings.evidence: Absence of any CI / bot configuration files at the repo root or under conventional paths; package.json scripts contain no 'audit' or 'snyk' / 'osv-scanner' step.
findings.recommendation: Add either (a) a GitHub Actions workflow running `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` on PR and weekly cron, or (b) enable Renovate / Dependabot with security-only updates auto-merged. Treat any high/critical advisory as a build failure.

findings.summary: No `engines` field — Node.js version is unconstrained. A developer or CI runner on a Node major Electron does not support will silently install incompatible native modules (serialport).
findings.recommendation: Add `"engines": {"node": ">=20.0.0 <23.0.0"}` matching the Node version bundled by the target Electron major, and `"engineStrict": true` in .npmrc to fail installs on mismatch.

findings.summary: No `overrides` field — when a transitive vulnerability lands with no upstream patch, there is no documented mechanism to force-pin the affected version.
findings.evidence: package.json declares dependencies and devDependencies only; no `overrides` / `resolutions` block. lockfileVersion 3 has hundreds of transitive packages with no override capability declared.
findings.recommendation: Add an empty `"overrides": {}` block now to mark policy intent, plus a runbook entry pointing at `npm overrides` for emergency transitive pinning.

findings.summary: Every direct dependency uses caret ranges (^) — when combined with no committed CI audit, a compromised maintainer release within an allowed minor/patch range will be installed silently on the next CI build.
findings.evidence: All 8 dependencies and all 15 devDependencies use ^ prefixes (e.g. "electron": "^31.0.0", "serialport": "^12.0.0"). The lockfile mitigates this locally but `npm ci` on a fresh clone with a regenerated lock will pick the latest in-range.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) pin to exact versions for runtime deps that ship in the app bundle (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `electron`, `electron-store`, `serialport`), letting Renovate propose bumps, or (b) keep ^ ranges but enforce `npm ci` (not `npm install`) in every build path and gate on lockfile diff in CI.

findings.summary: electron-store ^8.0.0 is one major behind — electron-store 9 went ESM-only. The pin to 8.x may be load-bearing for the current CommonJS main process; either way, security fixes published only to 9+ are unreachable.
findings.evidence: dependencies['electron-store'] = ^8.0.0; the v8→v9 boundary is the ESM transition.
findings.recommendation: If the main process is migrating to ESM, bump to 9+ at the same time. Otherwise document that electron-store is intentionally pinned to the last CJS major and watch its release notes for backported security fixes.

scoring.method: Same as security: fingerprint match first, then loose match by (file, category). Line numbers do not apply — these findings are file-level.
